docs.title: CIOOS Metadata Conversion
docs.text: Welcome to the documentation for CIOOS Metadata Conversion, a comprehensive tool for converting ocean metadata records between various international standards and formats.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This project provides a robust solution for transforming metadata from the CIOOS (Canadian Integrated Ocean Observing System) metadata entry form into widely recognized international metadata standards. It facilitates data sharing, discovery, and citation by bridging the gap between the CIOOS metadata profile and global metadata standards.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Multiple Output Formats: Convert to ISO 19115-3 XML, DataCite JSON/XML, ERDDAP/ACDD attributes, Citation.cff, and more
  • Bidirectional Support: Works with both CIOOS intermediate format and Firebase-based form data
  • Bilingual Metadata: Full support for English and French metadata
  • Automated Enrichment: Automatic translation of EOV codes, license resolution, coordinate transformations
  • CLI and Python API: Use as a command-line tool or integrate into your Python applications
  • Extensible Design: Easy to add new output formats and transformations

docs.title: Input Schemas
docs.text:
• CIOOS: The canonical CIOOS intermediate format
  • Firebase: Direct from CIOOS metadata entry form

docs.title: Output Formats
docs.text: Format Description Use Case iso19115-3_xml ISO 19115-3:2016 Geographic Information Metadata Standard for geospatial metadata, catalog harvesting datacite_xml DataCite Metadata Schema 4.5 XML Research data citation, DOI registration datacite_json DataCite Metadata Schema 4.5 JSON Programmatic data citation erddap ERDDAP datasets.xml attributes ERDDAP data server integration acdd_json ACDD 1.3 global attributes (JSON) NetCDF Climate and Forecast conventions acdd_yaml ACDD 1.3 global attributes (YAML) Human-readable ACDD attributes cff Citation File Format Software and dataset citation json CIOOS intermediate format (JSON) Data exchange, processing yaml CIOOS intermediate format (YAML) Human-readable format

docs.title: Quick Example
docs.text:
# Convert a CIOOS intermediate format record to ISO 19115-3 XML
cioos_metadata_conversion convert \
  --input record.yaml \
  --input-schema CIOOS \
  --output-format iso19115-3_xml \
  --output-file record.xml

# Convert Firebase JSON to DataCite XML
cioos_metadata_conversion convert \
  --input firebase-record.json \
  --input-schema firebase \
  --output-format datacite_xml \
  --output-file datacite.xml

docs.title: Python API Example
docs.text:
from cioos_metadata_conversion.record import Record

# Load and convert a record
record = Record(source="record.yaml", schema="CIOOS")
record.load().convert_to_cioos_schema()

# Convert to different formats
iso_xml = record.convert_to("iso19115-3_xml")
datacite_json = record.convert_to("datacite_json")
acdd_attrs = record.convert_to("acdd_yaml")

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
The conversion process follows a two-stage pipeline:

  1. Input to CIOOS: Source data (Firebase or CIOOS) → CIOOS intermediate format
  2. CIOOS to Output: CIOOS intermediate format → Target standard
graph LR
    A[CIOOS Form<br/>Firebase] --> C[CIOOS<br/>Intermediate Format]
    C --> D[ISO 19115-3 XML]
    C --> E[DataCite XML/JSON]
    C --> F[ERDDAP/ACDD]
    C --> G[Citation.cff]

This two-stage approach ensures:

  • Consistency: Single source of truth for transformations
  • Maintainability: Changes to standards only affect one conversion path
  • Extensibility: New formats only need to convert from CIOOS intermediate format

docs.text:

  • Ocean Data and Information Network (ODIN)
  • Global Change Master Directory (GCMD)

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: This document describes the architecture and design of the CIOOS Metadata Conversion tool.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The tool follows a two-stage conversion pipeline architecture:

Input Format → CIOOS Intermediate Format → Output Format

This design provides several benefits:

  • Consistency: Single source of truth for all conversions
  • Maintainability: Changes to standards only affect one conversion path
  • Extensibility: New formats only need to convert from/to CIOOS intermediate
  • Testability: Each stage can be tested independently

docs.title: System Architecture
docs.text:
graph TB
    A[CIOOS Form<br/>Firebase JSON] --> B[firebase_to_cioos.py]
    C[CIOOS<br/>Intermediate Format] --> D[Record Class]
    B --> D
    D --> E[CIOOS Intermediate<br/>Format]
    E --> F[metadata-xml<br/>Jinja2 Templates]
    E --> G[datacite.py]
    E --> H[acdd.py / erddap.py]
    E --> I[citation_cff.py]
    F --> J[ISO 19115-3 XML]
    G --> K[DataCite XML/JSON]
    H --> L[ERDDAP/ACDD]
    I --> M[Citation.cff]

docs.title: firebase_to_cioos.py
docs.text:
Transforms CIOOS Form (Firebase) exports to CIOOS intermediate format.

Responsibilities: - Field restructuring - Type conversions - Data enrichment (licenses, EOV translations) - Coordinate transformations - Contact processing - Empty value removal

Key Functions: - record_json_to_yaml(record): Main transformation function - fix_lat_long_polygon(polygon): Coordinate transformation - format_taxa(taxa): Taxa keyword flattening - eovs_to_fr(eovs_en): EOV translation

docs.title: record.py
docs.text:
Main interface for loading and converting metadata records.

Classes: - Record: Handles loading, schema conversion, and output generation - InputSchemas: Enum of supported input schemas - OUTPUT_FORMATS: Dict mapping format names to converter functions

Methods: - load(): Load metadata from file, URL, or dict - convert_to_cioos_schema(): Convert input to CIOOS intermediate - convert_to(format): Convert to target format

docs.title: 2. CIOOS Intermediate Format
docs.text:
The canonical representation used for all conversions.

Structure: 

metadata:      # About the metadata
spatial:       # Geographic extent
identification: # Resource description
contact:       # Responsible parties
distribution:  # Access information
platform:      # Platform/instruments (optional)

Features: - Bilingual support throughout - Normalized data types - Clean, minimal structure (no empty values) - Self-contained (includes all needed lookups)

docs.title: xml.py + metadata-xml
docs.text:
Generates ISO 19115-3 XML using Jinja2 templates.

External Dependency: metadata-xml package from GitHub

Process: 1. Load CIOOS record 2. Pass to Jinja2 template 3. Render XML 4. Indent and format

Key Templates (in metadata-xml repo): - main.j2: Main template - contact.j2: Responsible party handling - bilingual.j2: Multilingual text macros

docs.title: datacite.py
docs.text:
Generates DataCite 4.5 metadata.

Outputs: XML and JSON formats

Key Functions: - to_xml(record): Generate DataCite XML - to_json(record): Generate DataCite JSON - _get_creators(record): Process creators - _get_contributors(record): Process contributors - _scrub_empty(obj): Clean empty values

Mappings: See CIOOS to DataCite

docs.title: acdd.py + erddap.py
docs.text:
Generates ACDD 1.3 attributes for ERDDAP and NetCDF.

acdd.py: - acdd(record): Generate ACDD attributes dict - acdd_json(record): JSON output - acdd_yaml(record): YAML output

erddap.py: - global_attributes(record): Generate ERDDAP XML - update_dataset_xml(): Update existing datasets.xml

Features: - Multilingual attribute support - Vocabulary-based keywords - Platform/instrument metadata

docs.title: citation_cff.py
docs.text:
Generates Citation File Format.

Uses: cffconvert library for CFF generation

docs.title: 1. Loading Phase
docs.text:
record = Record(source="record.yaml", schema="CIOOS")
record.load()

Process: 1. Detect source type (file, URL, dict) 2. Load data (JSON or YAML) 3. Store in record.metadata

docs.title: 2. Schema Conversion
docs.text:
record.convert_to_cioos_schema()

For CIOOS Schema: - No conversion needed - Data already in correct format

For Firebase Schema: - Call firebase_to_cioos.record_json_to_yaml() - Transform structure, enrich data - Store result in record.metadata

docs.title: 3. Output Generation
docs.text:
xml = record.convert_to("iso19115-3_xml")

Process: 1. Lookup converter in OUTPUT_FORMATS dict 2. Pass record.metadata to converter 3. Generate and return output string

docs.title: Adding New Input Schema
docs.text:
1. Add to InputSchemas enum
  2. Create conversion function
  3. Update convert_to_cioos_schema() method
  4. Add tests

docs.title: Adding New Output Format
docs.text:
1. Create converter module (e.g., my_format.py)
  2. Add to OUTPUT_FORMATS dict in record.py
  3. Document mapping in docs/mappings/
  4. Add tests

Example:

# cioos_metadata_conversion/my_format.py
def to_my_format(record: dict) -> str:
    """Convert CIOOS record to My Format."""
    # Implementation
    pass

# cioos_metadata_conversion/record.py
OUTPUT_FORMATS = {
    # ...existing formats...
    "my_format": my_format.to_my_format,
}

docs.title: Modifying Transformations
docs.text:
For Firebase → CIOOS: Edit firebase_to_cioos.py

For CIOOS → ISO 19115-3: Edit templates in metadata-xml repo

For CIOOS → DataCite: Edit datacite.py

For CIOOS → ACDD/ERDDAP: Edit acdd.py or erddap.py

docs.title: Why Two-Stage Pipeline?
docs.text:
Alternatives Considered: - Direct conversion (Firebase → each standard) - Multi-stage pipeline with multiple intermediates

Chosen Approach: Two-stage via CIOOS intermediate

Rationale: - Simplicity: One intermediate format vs. many - Maintainability: Changes isolated to one conversion - Extensibility: Easy to add formats - Testability: Test each stage independently

docs.title: Why External metadata-xml Package?
docs.text: Rationale: - ISO 19115-3 is complex - Separate package allows independent updates - Reusable by other projects - Jinja2 templates easier to maintain than code

docs.title: Why Not Use XML Libraries for ISO 19115-3?
docs.text: Rationale: - Jinja2 templates more readable - Easier for non-developers to modify - Clear separation of data and presentation - Better handling of optional elements

docs.title: Bottlenecks
docs.text:
1. XML Generation: Jinja2 rendering can be slow for large records
  2. File I/O: Loading many records from disk
  3. JSON Parsing: Large Firebase exports

docs.title: Optimizations
docs.text:
• Use scrub_dict() to remove empty values early
  • Cache resource file loads (licenses, EOV, EPSG)
  • Batch processing for multiple files

docs.title: Scalability
docs.text: Current: Suitable for ~10,000 records Bottleneck: Memory for large batches Solution: Process in chunks or use streaming

docs.title: CIOOS Form Schema
docs.text: The CIOOS Form is a web-based metadata entry interface built on Firebase that allows researchers and data managers to create standardized metadata records for ocean datasets. This document describes the structure and fields of the CIOOS Form schema.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The CIOOS Form (also called the CIOOS Metadata Entry Form) is:

  • Web-based: Accessible at https://cioos-siooc.github.io/metadata-entry-form
  • Bilingual: Supports English and French metadata entry
  • Firebase-backed: Data stored in Firebase Realtime Database
  • Standards-aligned: Designed to capture data for multiple metadata standards

docs.title: Form URL Structure
docs.text:
https://cioos-siooc.github.io/metadata-entry-form#/{language}/{region}/{userID}/{recordID}
  • language: en or fr
  • region: Regional identifier (e.g., stlaurent, pacific, atlantic)
  • userID: Firebase user identifier
  • recordID: Unique record identifier

docs.title: Top-Level Fields
docs.text:
The CIOOS Form schema is a flat JSON structure with the following main sections:

{
  "identifier": "uuid",
  "recordID": "firebase-record-id",
  "userID": "firebase-user-id",
  "region": "stlaurent",
  "language": "en",
  "created": "2025-06-25T17:24:48.469Z",
  "title": {...},
  "abstract": {...},
  "contacts": [...],
  "map": {...},
  "keywords": {...},
  "eov": [...],
  "taxa": [...],
  "distribution": [...],
  "history": [...],
  "projects": [...],
  ...
}

docs.title: identifier
docs.text: Type: String (UUID) Required: Yes Description: Unique identifier for the metadata record Example: "9d1a8fe4-2675-4e34-8b65-16459736535a"

docs.title: datasetIdentifier
docs.text: Type: String (DOI URL) Required: No Description: Persistent identifier for the dataset (usually a DOI) Example: "https://doi.org/10.26071/mxtr-gp72"

docs.title: recordID
docs.text: Type: String Description: Firebase record ID Example: "-OTS9E-8LKZrL_Yuggg0"

docs.title: userID
docs.text: Type: String Description: Firebase user ID of record creator Example: "Ea7wMTBNmvWBD2n1oSc8X0KQi9z1"

docs.title: region
docs.text: Type: String Values: "stlaurent", "pacific", "atlantic", "hakai" Description: CIOOS regional node

docs.title: language
docs.text: Type: String Values: "en" or "fr" Description: Primary language of the metadata

docs.title: created
docs.text: Type: String (ISO 8601 datetime) Description: Last modification timestamp Example: "2025-06-25T17:24:48.469Z"

docs.title: title
docs.text:
Type: Bilingual object Required: Yes Structure: 

{
  "title": {
    "en": "English Title",
    "fr": "Titre français",
    "translations": {
      "en": {
        "message": "translation note",
        "verified": false
      }
    }
  }
}

docs.title: abstract
docs.text: Type: Bilingual object Required: Yes Description: Dataset description/summary Structure: Same as title with en and fr keys Supports: Markdown formatting

docs.title: edition
docs.text: Type: String Description: Version or edition of the dataset Example: "1.0.0"

docs.title: comment
docs.text: Type: Bilingual object or String Description: Additional comments about the dataset

docs.title: limitations
docs.text: Type: Bilingual object or String Description: Limitations or constraints on data use

docs.title: contacts
docs.text:
Type: Array of contact objects Required: Yes (at least one) Structure: 

{
  "contacts": [
    {
      "role": ["owner", "pointOfContact"],
      "inCitation": true,
      "givenNames": "FirstName",
      "lastName": "LastName",
      "indPosition": "Position Title",
      "indEmail": "person@example.org",
      "indOrcid": "https://orcid.org/0000-0000-0000-0000",
      "orgName": "Organization Name",
      "orgEmail": "org@example.org",
      "orgURL": "https://example.org",
      "orgAdress": "123 Street",
      "orgCity": "City",
      "orgCountry": "Canada",
      "orgRor": "https://ror.org/..."
    }
  ]
}

Contact Roles: - owner: Data owner - pointOfContact: Point of contact - custodian: Metadata custodian - distributor: Data distributor - publisher: Publisher - principalInvestigator: Principal investigator - processor: Data processor - originator: Originator - author: Author - coAuthor: Co-author - collaborator: Collaborator - contributor: Contributor - editor: Editor - funder: Funder - sponsor: Sponsor - rightsHolder: Rights holder - stakeholder: Stakeholder - mediator: Mediator - resourceProvider: Resource provider

docs.title: organization
docs.text: Type: String Description: Optional top-level organization name Note: If provided, creates an additional contact with owner role

docs.title: map
docs.text:
Type: Object Required: Yes Structure: 

{
  "map": {
    "west": "-125.0",
    "east": "-124.0",
    "south": "48.0",
    "north": "49.0",
    "polygon": "48.0,-125.0 48.0,-124.0 49.0,-124.0 49.0,-125.0",
    "description": {
      "en": "Geographic area name",
      "fr": "Nom de la zone géographique"
    },
    "descriptionIdentifier": "uuid"
  }
}

Note: Either bounding box (west/east/south/north) OR polygon is required Coordinate Format: Strings, polygon in "lat,long" format (transformed during conversion)

docs.title: verticalExtentMin
docs.text: Type: String (numeric) Description: Minimum depth/height Example: "0"

docs.title: verticalExtentMax
docs.text: Type: String (numeric) Description: Maximum depth/height Example: "100"

docs.title: verticalExtentDirection
docs.text: Type: String Values: "heightPositive" or "depthPositive" Description: Vertical coordinate direction

docs.title: verticalExtentEPSG
docs.text: Type: String Description: EPSG code for vertical reference system Example: "5829"

docs.title: noVerticalExtent
docs.text: Type: Boolean Description: Flag indicating no vertical extent applies

docs.title: dateStart
docs.text: Type: String (ISO 8601 datetime) Description: Start of temporal coverage Example: "2025-01-01T17:00:00.000Z"

docs.title: dateEnd
docs.text: Type: String (ISO 8601 datetime) Description: End of temporal coverage Example: "2025-03-01T17:00:00.000Z"

docs.title: timeFirstPublished
docs.text: Type: String (ISO 8601 datetime) Description: Date dataset was first published

docs.title: datePublished
docs.text: Type: String (ISO 8601 datetime) Description: Publication date

docs.title: dateRevised
docs.text: Type: String (ISO 8601 datetime) Description: Last revision date

docs.title: keywords
docs.text:
Type: Bilingual object with arrays Structure: 

{
  "keywords": {
    "en": ["keyword1", "keyword2", "keyword3"],
    "fr": ["mot-clé1", "mot-clé2", "mot-clé3"]
  }
}

docs.title: eov
docs.text:
Type: Array of strings Description: Essential Ocean Variables (EOV) from GOOS vocabulary Values: Camel-case codes (e.g., "oxygen", "invertebrateAbundanceAndDistribution") Example: 

{
  "eov": ["oxygen", "nutrients", "seaSurfaceTemperature"]
}

docs.title: taxa
docs.text:
Type: Array of GBIF taxonomy objects Description: Taxonomic information from GBIF Structure: 

{
  "taxa": [
    {
      "kingdom": "Animalia",
      "phylum": "Mollusca",
      "class": "Gastropoda",
      "order": "Stylommatophora",
      "family": "Helicidae",
      "genus": "Helix",
      "species": "Helix pomatia",
      "canonicalName": "Helix pomatia",
      "scientificName": "Helix pomatia Linnaeus, 1758",
      "key": 1234567,
      "rank": "SPECIES"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: noTaxa
docs.text: Type: Boolean Description: Flag indicating taxa information is not applicable

docs.title: projects
docs.text: Type: Array of strings Description: Associated research projects Example: ["Coastal Environmental Baseline Program", "Ocean Observing Initiative"]

docs.title: progress
docs.text: Type: String Values: "completed", "onGoing", "planned", "obsolete", "historicalArchive", etc. Description: Dataset progress/status code

docs.title: status
docs.text: Type: String Description: Publication workflow status

docs.title: metadataScope
docs.text: Type: String Values: "Dataset", "Series", "Service", etc. Description: Type of resource being described

docs.title: metadataScopeIso
docs.text: Type: String Description: ISO version of metadata scope

docs.title: distribution
docs.text:
Type: Array of distribution objects Structure: 

{
  "distribution": [
    {
      "url": "https://example.org/data",
      "name": {
        "en": "Distribution Name",
        "fr": "Nom de distribution"
      },
      "description": {
        "en": "Description...",
        "fr": "Description..."
      }
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: license
docs.text: Type: String Values: License code (e.g., "CC-BY-4.0", "CC-BY-NC-4.0", "CC0") Description: Data license code Resolved: To full license information via lookup table

docs.title: history
docs.text:
Type: Array of history objects Description: Provenance and processing history Structure: 

{
  "history": [
    {
      "scope": "Dataset",
      "statement": {
        "en": "History statement...",
        "fr": "Déclaration historique..."
      },
      "additionalDocumentation": [
        {
          "code": "https://example.org/doc",
          "title": {"en": "Doc Title"},
          "authority": "URL"
        }
      ],
      "source": [...],
      "processingStep": [...]
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: associated_resources
docs.text:
Type: Array of resource objects Description: Related datasets, publications, etc. Structure: 

{
  "associated_resources": [
    {
      "association_type": "IsReferencedBy",
      "association_type_iso": "crossReference",
      "authority": "DOI",
      "code": "https://doi.org/10.1002/example",
      "title": {
        "en": "Related Publication Title"
      }
    }
  ]
}

Association Types: - IsReferencedBy: This dataset is referenced by the resource - IsCitedBy: This dataset is cited by the resource - IsSupplementTo: This dataset supplements the resource - IsPartOf: This dataset is part of the resource

docs.title: platforms
docs.text:
Type: Array of platform objects Structure: 

{
  "platforms": [
    {
      "id": "platform-uuid",
      "name": {"en": "Platform Name"},
      "type": "coastal structure",
      "description": {"en": "Platform description"},
      "authority": {"en": "Authority name"},
      "role": "originator"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: instruments
docs.text:
Type: Array of instrument objects Structure: 

{
  "instruments": [
    {
      "id": "instrument-uuid",
      "type": {"en": "Sensor Type"},
      "description": {"en": "Instrument description"},
      "platform": "platform-uuid"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: noPlatform
docs.text: Type: Boolean Description: Flag indicating no platform information applies

docs.title: doiCreationStatus
docs.text: Type: String Values: "draft", "published" Description: DOI creation workflow status

docs.title: filename
docs.text: Type: String Description: Associated filename (if any)

docs.text:
Type: Object Structure: 

{
  "lastEditedBy": {
    "displayName": "User Name",

docs.text: Type: String Description: Internal categorization

docs.text: Type: Array of strings Description: Type of resource (e.g., ["biological"], ["physical"])

docs.title: Translation Object Structure
docs.text:
Bilingual fields can include translation metadata:

{
  "title": {
    "en": "Original English",
    "fr": "Traduction française",
    "translations": {
      "fr": {
        "message": "text translated using the Amazon translate service / texte traduit à l'aide du service de traduction Amazon",
        "verified": false
      }
    }
  }
}
  • message: Note about translation method
  • verified: Whether translation has been verified by a human

docs.title: Required Fields
docs.text:
At form submission, the following are typically required:

  • identifier
  • language
  • title (at least one language)
  • abstract (at least one language)
  • contacts (at least one with required fields)
  • map (bounding box or polygon)

docs.title: Conditional Requirements
docs.text:
• If noPlatform is false, platform information should be provided
  • If noTaxa is false, taxa information should be provided
  • Either bounding box OR polygon is required (not both)
  • At least one contact must have owner role

docs.title: Auto-save
docs.text: The form auto-saves to Firebase as users type, preventing data loss.

docs.title: URL-based Routing
docs.text: The form uses URL hash fragments for navigation: - Record selection - Form sections - Language switching

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: Client-side validation ensures: - Required fields are filled - Valid email formats - Valid URLs (DOI, ORCID, ROR) - Geographic coordinates in valid ranges

docs.title: Export Format
docs.text:
When exported from Firebase, records are JSON objects with the structure described above. These exports can be converted using:

cioos_metadata_conversion convert \
  --input firebase-export.json \
  --input-schema firebase \
  --output-format iso19115-3_xml

docs.text:
The form schema evolves over time. Key versions:

  • v1: Initial implementation
  • v2: Added platform/instrument support
  • v3: Enhanced lineage/history
  • Current: See form source code for latest

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text: The CIOOS Metadata Conversion tool provides a command-line interface (CLI) for converting metadata records between different formats and standards.

docs.title: Main Command
docs.text: cioos_metadata_conversion [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

docs.title: Global Options
docs.text: • --help: Show help message and exit

docs.title: convert
docs.text: Convert metadata records to different metadata formats or standards.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: cioos_metadata_conversion convert [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Required Options
docs.text: Option Short Type Description --input -i PATH Input file or URL --input-schema CHOICE Input file schema: CIOOS or firebase --output-format -f CHOICE Output format (see Output Formats)

docs.title: Optional Options
docs.text: Option Short Type Default Description --recursive -r FLAG false Process files recursively --encoding TEXT utf-8 Encoding of the input file --output-dir -p PATH . Output directory --output-file -o PATH Output file (single file only) --output-encoding TEXT utf-8 Encoding of the output file

docs.title: Output Formats
docs.text:
Available output format values for --output-format:

Format Description json CIOOS intermediate format (JSON) yaml CIOOS intermediate format (YAML) erddap ERDDAP datasets.xml attributes cff Citation File Format xml ISO 19115-3 XML (deprecated, use iso19115-3_xml) iso19115_xml ISO 19115-3 XML (deprecated, use iso19115-3_xml) iso19115-3_xml ISO 19115-3 XML datacite_json DataCite JSON datacite_xml DataCite XML acdd_json ACDD 1.3 attributes (JSON) acdd_yaml ACDD 1.3 attributes (YAML)

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Convert a single CIOOS intermediate format file to ISO 19115-3 XML:

cioos_metadata_conversion convert \
  --input record.yaml \
  --input-schema CIOOS \
  --output-format iso19115-3_xml \
  --output-file record.xml

Convert Firebase JSON to DataCite XML:

cioos_metadata_conversion convert \
  --input firebase-export.json \
  --input-schema firebase \
  --output-format datacite_xml \
  --output-dir ./output

Batch convert multiple YAML files:

cioos_metadata_conversion convert \
  --input "records/*.yaml" \
  --input-schema CIOOS \
  --output-format datacite_json \
  --output-dir ./datacite-output

Recursive directory processing:

cioos_metadata_conversion convert \
  --input "data/**/*.yaml" \
  --recursive \
  --input-schema CIOOS \
  --output-format iso19115-3_xml \
  --output-dir ./xml-output

Convert from URL:

cioos_metadata_conversion convert \
  --input "https://example.com/metadata.yaml" \
  --input-schema CIOOS \
  --output-format datacite_xml \
  --output-file output.xml

Specify custom encoding:

cioos_metadata_conversion convert \
  --input record.yaml \
  --encoding utf-8 \
  --input-schema CIOOS \
  --output-format iso19115-3_xml \
  --output-file record.xml \
  --output-encoding utf-8

docs.title: erddap-update
docs.text:
Update ERDDAP datasets.xml files with CIOOS metadata.

This command updates existing ERDDAP dataset configurations with metadata from CIOOS records. It matches datasets by URL and updates the global attributes.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: cioos_metadata_conversion erddap-update [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Short Type Required Description --datasets-xml -d PATH Yes Path to ERDDAP datasets.xml file --records -r PATH Yes Path to CIOOS records (glob pattern) --erddap-url -u TEXT Yes Base URL of the ERDDAP server --output -o PATH No Output file (default: updates in place) --backup FLAG No Create backup before updating --multilingual FLAG No Include multilingual attributes

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Update ERDDAP datasets.xml with CIOOS metadata:

cioos_metadata_conversion erddap-update \
  --datasets-xml /path/to/datasets.xml \
  --records "records/*.yaml" \
  --erddap-url "https://data.example.org/erddap" \
  --multilingual

Create backup and update:

cioos_metadata_conversion erddap-update \
  --datasets-xml /path/to/datasets.xml \
  --records "records/*.yaml" \
  --erddap-url "https://data.example.org/erddap" \
  --backup \
  --output /path/to/updated-datasets.xml

Update from Firebase records:

cioos_metadata_conversion erddap-update \
  --datasets-xml /path/to/datasets.xml \
  --records "firebase/*.json" \
  --erddap-url "https://data.example.org/erddap"

docs.title: Exit Codes
docs.text:
The CLI uses standard exit codes:

  • 0: Success
  • 1: General error (e.g., file not found, conversion failed)
  • 2: Command-line usage error

docs.title: CIOOS_LOG_LEVEL
docs.text:
Set the logging level:

export CIOOS_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG
cioos_metadata_conversion convert --input record.yaml ...

Valid values: DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL

docs.title: CIOOS_ENCODING
docs.text:
Default encoding for input/output files:

export CIOOS_ENCODING=utf-8

docs.title: Piping and Redirection
docs.text:
While the CLI doesn't support stdin directly, you can work with files:

# Convert and view output
cioos_metadata_conversion convert \
  --input record.yaml \
  --input-schema CIOOS \
  --output-format json | jq .

# Chain conversions
cioos_metadata_conversion convert \
  --input record.yaml \
  --input-schema CIOOS \
  --output-format json \
  --output-file temp.json

cioos_metadata_conversion convert \
  --input temp.json \
  --input-schema CIOOS \
  --output-format datacite_xml \
  --output-file final.xml

docs.title: Globbing Patterns
docs.text:
The CLI supports glob patterns for batch processing:

# All YAML files in current directory
cioos_metadata_conversion convert --input "*.yaml" ...

# All files recursively
cioos_metadata_conversion convert --input "**/*.yaml" --recursive ...

# Specific pattern
cioos_metadata_conversion convert --input "records/dataset-*.json" ...

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The CLI uses loguru for logging. Errors are logged to stderr:

# Capture errors
cioos_metadata_conversion convert ... 2> errors.log

# Verbose output
cioos_metadata_conversion convert ... 2>&1 | tee output.log

docs.title: Bash
docs.text:
Add to your ~/.bashrc:

eval "$(_CIOOS_METADATA_CONVERSION_COMPLETE=bash_source cioos_metadata_conversion)"

docs.title: Zsh

Add to your ~/.zshrc:

docs.title: Tips and Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Use Absolute Paths: When processing multiple files, use absolute paths to avoid confusion
  2. Test First: Try conversion on a single file before batch processing
  3. Check Encodings: Ensure input and output encodings match your data
  4. Validate Output: Always validate generated XML/JSON against schemas
  5. Use Output Directories: For batch processing, specify an output directory rather than individual files
  6. Backup Originals: When updating files (like ERDDAP), always create backups first

docs.title: Input Schemas
docs.text: The CIOOS Metadata Conversion tool supports two input schemas: CIOOS intermediate format and Firebase (CIOOS Form) exports.

docs.title: CIOOS Intermediate Format
docs.text: The canonical format used internally by the conversion tool. This is a structured YAML or JSON representation that serves as the source for all output conversions.

docs.title: Format: YAML or JSON
docs.text:
Both YAML and JSON representations are supported:

# record.yaml
metadata:
  naming_authority: ca.cioos
  identifier: uuid-here
  language: en
identification:
  title:
    en: "Dataset Title"
  abstract:
    en: "Description..."

{
  "metadata": {
    "naming_authority": "ca.cioos",
    "identifier": "uuid-here",
    "language": "en"
  },
  "identification": {
    "title": {"en": "Dataset Title"},
    "abstract": {"en": "Description..."}
  }
}

docs.title: Structure
docs.text: The CIOOS format has four main sections:

docs.title: metadata
docs.text: Metadata about the metadata record itself: - naming_authority: Authority for identifiers (typically "ca.cioos") - identifier: Unique metadata record identifier - language: Primary language ("en" or "fr") - dates: Publication and revision dates - use_constraints: License and limitations

docs.title: spatial
docs.text: Geographic and vertical extent: - bbox: Bounding box [west, south, east, north] - polygon: WKT polygon string - vertical: Vertical extent [min, max] - description: Geographic description

docs.title: identification
docs.text: Resource identification and description: - title: Bilingual title - identifier: Dataset identifier (e.g., DOI) - abstract: Bilingual abstract - keywords: Keywords by vocabulary (default, eov, taxa) - dates: Creation, publication, revision dates - temporal_begin/end: Temporal coverage - project: Associated projects - progress_code: Status (completed, onGoing, etc.)

docs.title: contact
docs.text:
Responsible parties: - roles: Array of roles (owner, distributor, etc.) - organization: Organization details - individual: Individual details (optional) - inCitation: Whether to include in citations

See the CIOOS Form to CIOOS mapping for complete structure details.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
cioos_metadata_conversion convert \
  --input record.yaml \
  --input-schema CIOOS \
  --output-format datacite_xml

docs.title: Firebase Format
docs.text: JSON export from the CIOOS metadata entry form. This format is automatically transformed to the CIOOS intermediate format during conversion.

docs.title: Format: JSON
docs.text:
Firebase exports are JSON files from the metadata entry form:

{
  "identifier": "uuid",
  "language": "en",
  "title": {
    "en": "Dataset Title",
    "fr": "Titre du jeu de données"
  },
  "abstract": {
    "en": "Description...",
    "fr": "Description..."
  },
  "contacts": [...],
  "map": {
    "west": "-125.0",
    "south": "48.0",
    "east": "-124.0",
    "north": "49.0"
  }
}

docs.title: Key Differences from CIOOS Format
docs.text:
1. Flat Structure: Firebase format is flatter than CIOOS
  2. String Coordinates: Geographic coordinates are strings, not floats
  3. Different Field Names: Uses form field names (e.g., datasetIdentifier vs identifier)
  4. Lat,Long Order: Polygon coordinates in lat,long order (transformed to long,lat)

docs.title: Transformation Process
docs.text:
Firebase format is automatically converted to CIOOS using firebase_to_cioos.record_json_to_yaml():

  1. Restructuring: Fields reorganized into CIOOS structure
  2. Type Conversion: Strings → floats for coordinates
  3. Coordinate Transform: lat,long → long,lat for polygons
  4. Enrichment: License codes resolved, EOVs translated
  5. Contact Processing: Contacts restructured, distributor auto-assigned

See the CIOOS Form to CIOOS mapping for complete transformation details.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
cioos_metadata_conversion convert \
  --input firebase-export.json \
  --input-schema firebase \
  --output-format iso19115-3_xml

docs.title: Loading from URLs
docs.text:
Both schemas support loading from URLs:

cioos_metadata_conversion convert \
  --input "https://example.com/metadata.yaml" \
  --input-schema CIOOS \
  --output-format datacite_xml

docs.title: When to Use CIOOS
docs.text:
• Working with already-processed metadata
  • Batch processing from a catalog
  • Integrating with other CIOOS tools
  • Maximum control over field values

docs.title: When to Use Firebase
docs.text:
• Direct exports from metadata entry form
  • Preserving form structure
  • Initial conversion from form to standards
  • Working with form backups

docs.title: CIOOS Format
docs.text: Required fields: - metadata.identifier - metadata.language - identification.title (with at least one language) - identification.abstract (with at least one language) - contact (at least one)

docs.title: Firebase Format
docs.text: Required fields: - identifier - language - title.en or title.fr - abstract.en or abstract.fr - contacts (at least one) - map with bounding box or polygon

docs.title: Minimal CIOOS Record
docs.text:
metadata:
  naming_authority: ca.cioos
  identifier: abc-123
  language: en
identification:
  title:
    en: "Minimal Dataset"
  abstract:
    en: "A minimal example"
spatial:
  bbox: [-125.0, 48.0, -124.0, 49.0]
contact:
  - roles: [owner]
    organization:
      name: "Example Org"

docs.title: Minimal Firebase Record
docs.text:
{
  "identifier": "abc-123",
  "language": "en",
  "title": {"en": "Minimal Dataset"},
  "abstract": {"en": "A minimal example"},
  "map": {
    "west": "-125.0",
    "south": "48.0",
    "east": "-124.0",
    "north": "49.0"
  },
  "contacts": [{
    "role": ["owner"],
    "orgName": "Example Org"
  }]
}

docs.title: Converting Between Schemas
docs.text:
To convert Firebase to CIOOS format:

cioos_metadata_conversion convert \
  --input firebase-export.json \
  --input-schema firebase \
  --output-format yaml \
  --output-file cioos-record.yaml

Then use the CIOOS format for subsequent conversions:

cioos_metadata_conversion convert \
  --input cioos-record.yaml \
  --input-schema CIOOS \
  --output-format datacite_xml

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: This guide will help you install the CIOOS Metadata Conversion package in your environment.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python: 3.11 or higher
  • Package Manager: pip or uv (recommended)

docs.title: Using pip (Standard)
docs.text:
Install directly from GitHub:

pip install git+https://github.com/cioos-siooc/cioos-metadata-conversion.git

docs.title: Using uv (Recommended)
docs.text:
uv is a fast Python package installer and resolver. It's recommended for development.

  1. Install uv:
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

Or on Windows:

powershell -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"
  1. Install the package:
uv pip install git+https://github.com/cioos-siooc/cioos-metadata-conversion.git

docs.title: Development Installation
docs.text:
For development or to contribute to the project:

  1. Clone the repository:
git clone https://github.com/cioos-siooc/cioos-metadata-conversion.git
cd cioos-metadata-conversion
  1. Install with uv (recommended):
# Install uv if you haven't already
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

# Sync dependencies
uv sync --dev

Or install with pip:

pip install -e ".[dev]"
  1. Verify installation:
cioos_metadata_conversion --help

docs.text: The package has the following main dependencies:

  • requests: HTTP library

docs.title: Verifying Installation
docs.text: After installation, verify that the package is working correctly:

docs.title: Check CLI Access
docs.text:
cioos_metadata_conversion --help

You should see output showing the available commands:

Usage: cioos_metadata_conversion [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

  CIOOS Metadata Conversion CLI.
  Convert metadata records to different metadata formats or standards.

Options:
  --help  Show this message and exit.

Commands:
  convert        Convert metadata records to different metadata formats...
  erddap-update  Update ERDDAP datasets.xml files with CIOOS metadata

docs.title: Test Basic Conversion
docs.text:
Create a test file and try converting it:

# Download a sample record (example)
curl -o sample.yaml https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cioos-siooc/cioos-metadata-conversion/main/tests/records/test_record1.yaml

# Convert to ISO 19115-3 XML
cioos_metadata_conversion convert \
  --input sample.yaml \
  --input-schema CIOOS \
  --output-format iso19115-3_xml \
  --output-file output.xml

# Check the output
cat output.xml

docs.text:
Test the Python API:

from cioos_metadata_conversion.record import Record, InputSchemas

docs.title: Module Not Found Errors
docs.text:
If you see ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'metadata_xml':

The metadata-xml package is installed from GitHub. Ensure your installation includes it:

pip install git+https://github.com/cioos-siooc/metadata-xml.git

Or reinstall the main package which should pull it in:

pip install --force-reinstall git+https://github.com/cioos-siooc/cioos-metadata-conversion.git

docs.title: Python Version Issues
docs.text:
Ensure you're using Python 3.11 or higher:

python --version

If you have multiple Python versions, use:

python3.11 -m pip install git+https://github.com/cioos-siooc/cioos-metadata-conversion.git

docs.title: Permission Errors
docs.text:
On Unix/Linux systems, if you encounter permission errors, use:

pip install --user git+https://github.com/cioos-siooc/cioos-metadata-conversion.git

Or use a virtual environment (recommended):

python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate  # On Windows: venv\Scripts\activate
pip install git+https://github.com/cioos-siooc/cioos-metadata-conversion.git

docs.title: Usage Guide
docs.text: This guide provides detailed examples and workflows for using the CIOOS Metadata Conversion tool.

docs.title: Understanding the Conversion Pipeline
docs.text:
The tool uses a two-stage conversion pipeline:

Input Format → CIOOS Intermediate Format → Output Format

This architecture ensures consistency and makes it easy to add new formats.

docs.title: CIOOS Intermediate Format
docs.text:
The canonical format used internally. It's a structured representation (YAML or JSON) optimized for conversion.

Example structure: 

metadata:
  naming_authority: ca.cioos
  identifier: uuid-here
  language: en
identification:
  title:
    en: "Dataset Title"
    fr: "Titre du jeu de données"
  abstract:
    en: "Dataset description..."
spatial:
  bbox: [-125.0, 48.0, -124.0, 49.0]
contact:
  - roles: [owner, distributor]
    organization:
      name: "Organization Name"

docs.title: Firebase Format
docs.text: JSON export from the CIOOS metadata entry form. This is automatically converted to CIOOS intermediate format.

docs.title: Single File Conversion
docs.text:
Convert one file to one output:

cioos_metadata_conversion convert \
  --input record.yaml \
  --input-schema CIOOS \
  --output-format iso19115-3_xml \
  --output-file record.xml

docs.title: Batch Conversion
docs.text:
Convert multiple files with glob patterns:

# All YAML files in a directory
cioos_metadata_conversion convert \
  --input "records/*.yaml" \
  --input-schema CIOOS \
  --output-format datacite_json \
  --output-dir ./datacite

# Recursive processing
cioos_metadata_conversion convert \
  --input "data/**/*.yaml" \
  --recursive \
  --input-schema CIOOS \
  --output-format iso19115-3_xml \
  --output-dir ./xml-output

docs.title: Format Conversion Chain
docs.text:
Convert between formats:

# Firebase → CIOOS intermediate format
cioos_metadata_conversion convert \
  -i firebase-export.json \
  --input-schema firebase \
  -f yaml \
  -o cioos-record.yaml

# CIOOS intermediate format → ISO 19115-3 XML
cioos_metadata_conversion convert \
  -i cioos-record.yaml \
  --input-schema CIOOS \
  -f iso19115-3_xml \
  -o record.xml

docs.title: Batch Processing in Python
docs.text:
from pathlib import Path
from cioos_metadata_conversion.record import Record

input_dir = Path("records")
output_dir = Path("output")
output_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

for yaml_file in input_dir.glob("*.yaml"):
    try:
        # Load record
        record = Record(source=str(yaml_file), schema="CIOOS")
        record.load().convert_to_cioos_schema()

        # Convert to DataCite XML
        datacite_xml = record.convert_to("datacite_xml")

        # Save output
        output_file = output_dir / f"{yaml_file.stem}.xml"
        output_file.write_text(datacite_xml)

        print(f"✓ Converted {yaml_file.name}")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"✗ Failed {yaml_file.name}: {e}")

from cioos_metadata_conversion.record import Record

except ValueError as e:
    logger.error(f"Invalid record: {e}")
except Exception as e:
    logger.exception("Conversion failed")

docs.title: Update ERDDAP datasets.xml
docs.text:
Automatically update ERDDAP configuration with CIOOS metadata:

cioos_metadata_conversion erddap-update \
  --datasets-xml /path/to/datasets.xml \
  --records "records/*.yaml" \
  --erddap-url "https://data.example.org/erddap" \
  --multilingual \
  --backup

What it does: 1. Matches CIOOS records to ERDDAP datasets by URL 2. Generates ACDD-compliant global attributes 3. Updates the datasets.xml file 4. Preserves existing configuration 5. Optionally creates backup

docs.text:

  -i cioos-records/*.yaml \
  --input-schema CIOOS \
  -f acdd_yaml \

# 2. Review generated attributes
cat acdd-attributes/dataset1.acdd_yaml

# 3. Update ERDDAP configuration
cioos_metadata_conversion erddap-update \
  -d /opt/erddap/datasets.xml \
  -r cioos-records/*.yaml \
  -u "https://data.example.org/erddap" \

docs.title: Quality Control Pipeline
docs.text:
#!/bin/bash
# validate-and-convert.sh

INPUT_DIR="source-records"
OUTPUT_DIR="validated-output"
ERROR_LOG="errors.log"

mkdir -p "$OUTPUT_DIR"

for record in "$INPUT_DIR"/*.yaml; do
    echo "Processing $record..."

    # Convert to ISO 19115-3 XML
    if cioos_metadata_conversion convert \
        -i "$record" \
        --input-schema CIOOS \
        -f iso19115-3_xml \
        -o "$OUTPUT_DIR/$(basename "$record" .yaml).xml" \
        2>> "$ERROR_LOG"; then
        echo "✓ Success"
    else
        echo "✗ Failed - check $ERROR_LOG"
    fi
done

docs.title: Multi-Format Export
docs.text:
Generate all formats for a record:

#!/bin/bash
# export-all-formats.sh

INPUT="record.yaml"
OUTPUT_DIR="exports"

mkdir -p "$OUTPUT_DIR"

formats=("iso19115-3_xml" "datacite_xml" "datacite_json" "acdd_yaml" "cff")

for format in "${formats[@]}"; do
    echo "Generating $format..."
    cioos_metadata_conversion convert \
        -i "$INPUT" \
        --input-schema CIOOS \
        -f "$format" \
        -p "$OUTPUT_DIR"
done

echo "All formats exported to $OUTPUT_DIR"

docs.title: Integration with CI/CD
docs.text:
# .github/workflows/convert-metadata.yml
name: Convert Metadata

on:
  push:
    paths:
      - 'metadata/*.yaml'

jobs:
  convert:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v4
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'

      - name: Install converter
        run: |
          pip install git+https://github.com/cioos-siooc/cioos-metadata-conversion.git

      - name: Convert to ISO 19115-3
        run: |
          cioos_metadata_conversion convert \
            -i "metadata/*.yaml" \
            --input-schema CIOOS \
            -f iso19115-3_xml \
            -p xml-output

      - name: Upload artifacts
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
        with:
          name: xml-metadata
          path: xml-output/

docs.text: Ensure your CIOOS records have required fields: - metadata.identifier - metadata.language - identification.title - identification.abstract - contact (at least one)

docs.title: 2. Use Appropriate Formats
docs.text:
• ISO 19115-3 XML: Geospatial catalogs, long-term archival
  • DataCite: DOI registration, citation

# Test first
cioos_metadata_conversion convert -i test-record.yaml ...

cioos_metadata_conversion convert -i "all-records/*.yaml" ...

cp -r records/ records-backup/

find records/ -name "*.yaml" | xargs -n 100 \

docs.text:
The CIOOS Metadata Conversion tool uses a two-stage pipeline:

graph LR
    A[CIOOS Form<br/>Firebase] -->|firebase_to_cioos.py| B[CIOOS<br/>Intermediate Format]
    B -->|metadata-xml| C[ISO 19115-3 XML]
    B -->|datacite.py| D[DataCite XML/JSON]
    B -->|acdd.py + erddap.py| E[ERDDAP/ACDD]

docs.title: Field Mapping Summary
docs.text:
NEW! Comprehensive table showing all CIOOS Form fields and how they map to each output format in a single view.

This is the best starting point if you want to see at a glance which fields are supported by which standards, including contact role mappings, language code conversions, and data transformation details.

docs.title: CIOOS Form to CIOOS
docs.text:
Documents the transformation from the CIOOS metadata entry form (Firebase export) to the canonical CIOOS intermediate format.

Key transformations: - Field restructuring and normalization - Coordinate transformations (lat,long → long,lat) - EOV translation (English → French) - Taxa keyword flattening - License code resolution - Contact restructuring - Automatic distributor assignment

docs.title: CIOOS to ISO 19115-3
docs.text:
Documents the generation of ISO 19115-3:2016 compliant XML metadata from the CIOOS intermediate format.

Standard: ISO 19115-3:2016 Geographic Information - Metadata Implementation: Via metadata-xml package using Jinja2 templates

Key features: - Bilingual metadata using PT_FreeText - Complete geographic extent support - Platform and instrument acquisition information - Resource lineage and history - Responsible party details with roles

docs.title: CIOOS to DataCite
docs.text:
Documents the mapping to DataCite Metadata Schema 4.5 for research data citation and DOI registration.

Standard: DataCite Metadata Schema v4.5 Output formats: XML and JSON

Key features: - DOI-focused metadata structure - Creator and contributor mappings - Funding information - Related identifiers - Geolocation support

docs.title: CIOOS to ERDDAP/ACDD
docs.text:
Documents the generation of ERDDAP global attributes following ACDD 1.3 conventions.

Standard: ACDD 1.3 (Attribute Convention for Data Discovery) Use case: ERDDAP data servers, NetCDF files

Key features: - CF conventions compliance - Vocabulary-based keywords - Platform and instrument metadata - Contact information as attributes - Multilingual attribute support

docs.title: Understanding Field Mappings
docs.text:
Each mapping document provides:

  1. Field-by-field mappings: Source → Target with processing logic
  2. Data types: Expected types and formats
  3. Required/optional indicators: Compliance requirements
  4. Default values: When fields are missing
  5. Special processing: Transformations, lookups, validations
  6. Examples: Sample input/output for clarity

docs.title: Bilingual Fields
docs.text:
Most text fields support bilingual content (English/French):

CIOOS Form: 

{
  "title": {
    "en": "English Title",
    "fr": "Titre français"
  }
}

CIOOS Intermediate: 

title:
  en: "English Title"
  fr: "Titre français"

ISO 19115-3 Output: 

<cit:title>
  <gco:CharacterString>English Title</gco:CharacterString>
  <lan:PT_FreeText>
    <lan:textGroup>
      <lan:LocalisedCharacterString locale="#en">English Title</lan:LocalisedCharacterString>
    </lan:textGroup>
    <lan:textGroup>
      <lan:LocalisedCharacterString locale="#fr">Titre français</lan:LocalisedCharacterString>
    </lan:textGroup>
  </lan:PT_FreeText>
</cit:title>

docs.title: Contact Information
docs.text:
Contacts are structured with organization and optional individual details:

CIOOS Intermediate: 

contact:
  - roles: [owner, distributor]
    organization:
      name: "Organization Name"
      ror: "https://ror.org/..."
    individual:
      name: "LastName, FirstName"
      orcid: "https://orcid.org/..."
    inCitation: true

This maps to appropriate structures in: - ISO 19115-3: CI_Responsibility with CI_Organisation or CI_Individual - DataCite: creators and contributors with affiliations - ACDD: creator_* and contributor_* attributes

docs.title: Geographic Extent
docs.text:
Spatial coverage can use bounding box or polygon:

CIOOS Intermediate: 

spatial:
  bbox: [-125.0, 48.0, -124.0, 49.0]  # [west, south, east, north]
  polygon: "-125.0,48.0 -124.0,48.0 -124.0,49.0 -125.0,49.0"

Maps to: - ISO 19115-3: EX_GeographicBoundingBox or EX_BoundingPolygon - DataCite: geoLocations with geoLocationBox or geoLocationPolygon - ACDD: geospatial_bounds and geospatial_* attributes

docs.title: Keywords and Vocabularies
docs.text:
Keywords are organized by vocabulary:

CIOOS Intermediate: 

identification:
  keywords:
    default:
      en: ["keyword1", "keyword2"]
    eov:
      en: ["oxygen", "nutrients"]
    taxa:
      en: ["Animalia", "Mollusca"]

Maps to: - ISO 19115-3: Multiple MD_Keywords blocks with thesaurus names - DataCite: subjects with optional subjectScheme - ACDD: Comma-separated keywords with prefixes and keywords_vocabulary

docs.title: CIOOS Form to CIOOS Intermediate Format Mapping
docs.text: This document describes how metadata fields from the CIOOS Form (Firebase-based) are transformed into the CIOOS intermediate format, which serves as the canonical representation for all subsequent conversions (ISO 19115-3, DataCite, ERDDAP/ACDD, etc.).

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The CIOOS Form is a web-based metadata entry interface that stores data in Firebase. The conversion to the intermediate CIOOS format is handled by the record_json_to_yaml() function in firebase_to_cioos.py.

docs.title: Transformation Purpose
docs.text: The CIOOS intermediate format: - Provides a clean, consistent structure for metadata - Removes empty values and normalizes data types - Performs coordinate transformations and data enrichment - Serves as the source for all output format conversions

docs.title: Key Processing Steps
docs.text:
1. Field Restructuring: Flatten and reorganize Firebase structure
  2. Data Enrichment: Resolve license codes, translate EOVs, format taxa
  3. Coordinate Transformation: Convert lat,long to long,lat format
  4. Date Normalization: Extract dates from datetime strings
  5. Contact Processing: Restructure contact information and add missing distributors
  6. Empty Value Removal: Scrub all empty strings, nulls, and empty objects

docs.title: Top-Level Structure
docs.text:
The CIOOS intermediate format has four main sections:

metadata:      # Metadata about the metadata
spatial:       # Geographic and vertical extent
identification: # Resource identification and description
contact:       # Responsible parties
distribution:  # Distribution/access information
platform:      # Platform and instrument information (optional)
instruments:   # Standalone instruments (optional)

docs.title: metadata.naming_authority
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: N/A Value: "ca.cioos" Processing: Hardcoded value Description: Authority responsible for creating the identifier

docs.title: metadata.identifier
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: identifier Type: String (UUID) Example: "9d1a8fe4-2675-4e34-8b65-16459736535a" Description: Unique identifier for the metadata record

docs.title: metadata.language
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: language Type: String Values: "en" | "fr" Description: Primary language of the metadata

docs.title: metadata.language_alternate
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: Derived (opposite of language) Processing: Not explicitly set but inferred Description: Alternate language for bilingual metadata

docs.title: metadata.maintenance_note
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: Constructed from userID, recordID, language, region Format: "Generated from https://cioos-siooc.github.io/metadata-entry-form#/{language}/{region}/{userID}/{recordID}" Example: "Generated from https://cioos-siooc.github.io/metadata-entry-form#/fr/stlaurent/Ea7wMTBNmvWBD2n1oSc8X0KQi9z1/-OTS9E-8LKZrL_Yuggg0" Description: Link back to the form where metadata was created

docs.title: metadata.use_constraints
docs.text:
CIOOS Form Source: Multiple sources Structure: 

use_constraints:
  limitations:
    en: "..."
    fr: "..."
  licence:
    title:
      en: "..."
    url: "..."
    code: "..."

docs.title: metadata.use_constraints.limitations
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: limitations Type: Bilingual text or string Default: "None" if not provided

docs.title: metadata.use_constraints.licence
docs.text:
CIOOS Form Source: license (code like "CC-BY-4.0") Processing: Resolved via licenses.json lookup Structure: - title.en: Full license name - url: License URL - code: License code Example: 

licence:
  title:
    en: "Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 Attribution"
  url: "https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0"
  code: "CC-BY-4.0"

docs.title: metadata.comment
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: comment Type: Bilingual text or string

docs.title: metadata.history
docs.text:
CIOOS Form Source: history array Type: Array of lineage objects Structure: Each history item includes: - statement: Bilingual text - scope: Scope code (e.g., "Dataset") - scopeIso: ISO scope code - additionalDocumentation: Array of citation objects - source: Array of source objects - processingStep: Array of processing step objects

Passed through: Structure preserved from form

docs.title: metadata.dates
docs.text:
CIOOS Form Source: Multiple date fields Structure: 

dates:
  revision: "2025-06-25T17:24:48.469Z"
  publication: "2025-01-01"

docs.title: metadata.dates.revision
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: created Type: ISO 8601 datetime string Description: Last modification timestamp

docs.title: metadata.dates.publication
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: timeFirstPublished Processing: date_from_datetime_str() - extracts date part (first 10 characters) Format: "YYYY-MM-DD" or empty Description: First publication date

docs.title: metadata.scope
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: metadataScopeIso OR metadataScope Type: String Values: "dataset", "series", "service", etc. Description: Type of resource being described

docs.title: spatial.bbox
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: map.west, map.south, map.east, map.north Type: Array of 4 floats [west, south, east, north] Condition: Only if map.polygon is NOT present Processing: Convert string values to floats Example: [-66.97, 49.91, -66.77, 50.04]

docs.title: spatial.polygon
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: map.polygon Type: String (space-separated coordinate pairs) Processing: fix_lat_long_polygon() - transforms from "lat,long" to "long,lat" Format: "long1,lat1 long2,lat2 long3,lat3 ..." Example Input: "50.03,-66.84 50.01,-66.93 49.97,-66.97" Example Output: "-66.84,50.03 -66.93,50.01 -66.97,49.97" Note: Polygon takes precedence over bbox if both exist

docs.title: spatial.vertical
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: verticalExtentMin, verticalExtentMax, noVerticalExtent Type: Array of 2 floats [min, max] Processing: - If noVerticalExtent is true: [0, 0] - Otherwise: [float(verticalExtentMin), float(verticalExtentMax)]

docs.title: spatial.vertical_positive
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: verticalExtentDirection or noVerticalExtent Type: String Values: "heightPositive" | "depthPositive" Default: "heightPositive" if noVerticalExtent is true

docs.title: spatial.vertical_epsg
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: verticalExtentEPSG or noVerticalExtent Processing: Resolved via epsg.json lookup Default: EPSG 5829 if noVerticalExtent is true Structure: Full EPSG definition object

docs.title: spatial.description
docs.text:
CIOOS Form Source: map.description Type: Bilingual text Example: 

description:
  en: "Port-Cartier"
  fr: "Port-Cartier"

docs.title: spatial.descriptionIdentifier
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: map.descriptionIdentifier Type: String (UUID) Description: Unique identifier for the geographic description

docs.title: identification.title
docs.text:
CIOOS Form Source: title Type: Bilingual text Example: 

title:
  en: "DCBA"
  fr: "ABCD"
  translations:
    en:
      message: "text translated using..."
      verified: false

docs.title: identification.identifier
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: datasetIdentifier Type: String (usually DOI) Example: "https://doi.org/10.26071/mxtr-gp72" Description: Persistent identifier for the dataset

docs.title: identification.abstract
docs.text:
CIOOS Form Source: abstract Type: Bilingual text Example: 

abstract:
  en: "Zyxwvutsrqponmi kjihgfedcba..."
  fr: "Abcdefghijk lmnopqrstuvwxyz..."

docs.title: identification.associated_resources
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: associated_resources Type: Array of resource objects Structure: Each resource includes: - association_type: DataCite-style type (e.g., "IsReferencedBy", "IsCitedBy") - association_type_iso: ISO-style type (e.g., "crossReference") - authority: Authority type ("DOI", "URL") - code: The identifier/URL - title: Bilingual title Passed through: Structure preserved from form

docs.title: identification.dates
docs.text:
CIOOS Form Source: Multiple date fields Structure: 

dates:
  creation: "2025-01-01"
  publication: "2025-01-01"
  revision: "2025-01-01"

docs.title: identification.dates.creation
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: dateStart Processing: date_from_datetime_str() - extracts date part Description: Dataset creation date

docs.title: identification.dates.publication
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: datePublished Processing: date_from_datetime_str() - extracts date part Description: Dataset publication date

docs.title: identification.dates.revision
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: dateRevised Processing: date_from_datetime_str() - extracts date part Description: Dataset revision date

docs.title: identification.keywords
docs.text:
CIOOS Form Source: keywords, eov, taxa Structure: 

keywords:
  default:
    en: ["keyword1", "keyword2"]
    fr: ["mot-clé1", "mot-clé2"]
  eov:
    en: ["oxygen", "nutrients"]
    fr: ["Oxygène", "Nutriments"]
  taxa:
    en: ["Animalia", "Mollusca"]
    fr: ["Animalia", "Mollusca"]

docs.title: identification.keywords.default
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: keywords.en and keywords.fr Processing: strip_keywords() - removes leading/trailing whitespace Type: Bilingual keyword lists

docs.title: identification.keywords.eov
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: eov array Processing: - English: Direct from form - French: eovs_to_fr() - translates using eov.json lookup Example: "invertebrateAbundanceAndDistribution" → "Abondance et distribution d'invertébrés"

docs.title: identification.keywords.taxa
docs.text:
CIOOS Form Source: taxa array (GBIF taxonomy objects) Processing: format_taxa() - flattens taxonomic hierarchy Logic: - Extracts: kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species - Joins non-null values with commas - Splits back into array of individual taxa names Example Input: 

{
  "kingdom": "Animalia",
  "phylum": "Mollusca",
  "class": "Gastropoda"
}
Example Output: ["Animalia", "Mollusca", "Gastropoda"]

Removal: If noTaxa is true, the entire taxa key is removed

docs.title: identification.temporal_begin
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: dateStart Type: ISO 8601 datetime string Description: Start of temporal coverage

docs.title: identification.temporal_end
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: dateEnd Type: ISO 8601 datetime string Description: End of temporal coverage

docs.title: identification.status
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: status Type: String Description: Dataset status (often used for publication workflow)

docs.title: identification.project
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: projects Type: Array of strings Example: ["Coastal Environmental Baseline Program"]

docs.title: identification.progress_code
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: progress Type: String Values: "completed", "onGoing", "planned", "obsolete", etc. Example: "completed"

docs.title: identification.edition
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: edition Type: String Description: Version or edition of the dataset

docs.title: Contact Section
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: contacts array Type: Array of contact objects Processing: Restructures each contact, adds automatic distributor

docs.title: Contact Structure
docs.text:
Each contact in the CIOOS format: 

- roles: ["owner", "funder"]
  organization:
    name: "Organization Name"
    url: "https://example.org"
    address: "123 Street"
    city: "City"
    country: "Country"
    email: "org@example.org"
    ror: "https://ror.org/..."
  individual:
    name: "LastName, FirstName"
    position: "Position Title"
    email: "person@example.org"
    orcid: "https://orcid.org/..."
  inCitation: true

docs.title: roles
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: contact.role Type: Array of strings Direct mapping: Roles passed through as-is

docs.title: organization.name
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: contact.orgName

docs.title: organization.url
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: contact.orgURL

docs.title: organization.address
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: contact.orgAdress Note: Typo in form field name preserved

docs.title: organization.city
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: contact.orgCity

docs.title: organization.country
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: contact.orgCountry

docs.title: organization.email
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: contact.orgEmail

docs.title: organization.ror
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: contact.orgRor Description: Research Organization Registry identifier

docs.title: individual.name
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: contact.lastName, contact.givenNames Processing: Concatenates as "LastName, FirstName" Logic: ", ".join([lastName, givenNames]) with None removal

docs.title: individual.position
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: contact.indPosition

docs.title: individual.email
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: contact.indEmail

docs.title: individual.orcid
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: contact.indOrcid Format: "https://orcid.org/0000-0000-0000-0000"

docs.title: inCitation
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: contact.inCitation Type: Boolean Description: Whether this contact should appear in dataset citations

docs.title: 1. Automatic Distributor Assignment
docs.text:
Logic (lines 296-303): 

# If there's no distributor set, set it to the data contact (owner)
all_roles = [contact["role"] for contact in record["contacts"]]
all_roles_flat = [j for sub in all_roles for j in sub]

if "distributor" not in all_roles_flat:
    for contact in record["contacts"]:
        if "owner" in contact["role"]:
            contact["role"] += ["distributor"]

Effect: If no contact has "distributor" role, it's automatically added to all "owner" contacts

docs.title: 2. Organization Contact Prepending
docs.text:
CIOOS Form Source: organization (top-level field) Logic (lines 305-313): 

if organization:
    organization = {
        "roles": ["owner"],
        "organization": {"name": record.get("organization")},
    }
    record_yaml["contact"] = [organization] + record_yaml["contact"]

Effect: If a top-level organization field exists, creates a new contact and prepends it to the contact list

docs.title: Distribution Section
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: distribution array Type: Array of distribution objects Structure Preserved: Each distribution object passed through with minimal processing

docs.title: Distribution Structure
docs.text:
distribution:
  - url: "https://example.org/data"
    name:
      en: "ERDDAP Dataset"
      fr: "Jeu de données ERDDAP"
    description:
      en: "Complete dataset..."
      fr: "Ensemble de données complet..."

docs.title: url
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: distribution[].url Type: String (URL)

docs.title: name
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: distribution[].name Type: Bilingual text

docs.title: description
docs.text: CIOOS Form Source: distribution[].description Type: Bilingual text

docs.title: Platform and Instruments Section
docs.text: Condition: Behavior depends on noPlatform flag

docs.title: Case 1: No Platform (noPlatform = true)
docs.text:
Result: instruments array at root level CIOOS Form Source: instruments Structure: Array passed through as-is

instruments:
  - id: "inst-1"
    type: "Sensor"
    description: "..."

docs.title: Case 2: Single Platform
docs.text:
Condition: platforms array has exactly 1 element Result: platform array with instruments nested Processing: 

record["platforms"][0]["instruments"] = instrumentsList
record_yaml["platform"] = record["platforms"]

Structure: 

platform:
  - id: "plat-1"
    name: "Platform Name"
    type: "coastal structure"
    instruments:
      - id: "inst-1"
        type: "Sensor"
      - id: "inst-2"
        type: "Profiler"

docs.title: Case 3: Multiple Platforms
docs.text:
Condition: platforms array has > 1 element Result: platform array with instruments matched by platform ID Processing: Each instrument's platform field matched to platform id

for platform in platformList:
    instruments = []
    for instrument in instrumentsList:
        if instrument["platform"] == platform["id"]:
            instruments.append(instrument)
    if len(instruments) > 0:
        platform["instruments"] = instruments

Structure: 

platform:
  - id: "plat-1"
    name: "Platform 1"
    instruments:
      - id: "inst-1"
  - id: "plat-2"
    name: "Platform 2"
    instruments:
      - id: "inst-2"
      - id: "inst-3"

docs.title: scrub_dict(d_in)
docs.text: Purpose: Recursively remove empty strings, None values, and empty objects Applied: To entire output structure Effect: Clean, minimal output without null pollution

docs.title: scrub_list(d_in)
docs.text: Purpose: Scrub dictionaries within lists Applied: To all array values

docs.title: strip_keywords(keywords)
docs.text: Purpose: Remove leading/trailing whitespace from keywords Input: {"en": ["keyword "], "fr": [" mot-clé"]} Output: {"en": ["keyword"], "fr": ["mot-clé"]}

docs.title: date_from_datetime_str(datetime_str)
docs.text: Purpose: Extract date from datetime string Input: "2025-01-01T17:00:00.000Z" Output: "2025-01-01" Logic: Returns first 10 characters

docs.title: fix_lat_long_polygon(polygon)
docs.text: Purpose: Transform coordinate order from lat,long to long,lat Input: "50.03,-66.84 50.01,-66.93" Output: "-66.84,50.03 -66.93,50.01" Steps: 1. Replace ", " with "," (clean spacing) 2. Split by spaces into coordinate pairs 3. For each pair, split by comma into [lat, long] 4. Rejoin as [long, lat]

docs.title: format_taxa(taxa)
docs.text: Purpose: Flatten GBIF taxonomy objects to keyword list Input: Array of taxonomy objects with hierarchical structure Output: Flat array of taxonomic names Logic: - Extract: kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species - Filter out None/null values - Join with commas, then split back to array Effect: Converts complex taxonomy to simple keyword list

docs.title: Fields Not Mapped
docs.text:
The following CIOOS Form fields are NOT included in the CIOOS intermediate format:

  • category - Internal categorization
  • doiCreationStatus - DOI workflow status
  • filename - Internal file tracking
  • lastEditedBy - Editor information
  • recordID - Firebase record ID (used only for maintenance_note URL)
  • region - Regional classification (used only for maintenance_note URL)
  • resourceType - Resource type classification
  • status - Mapped but often empty/unused
  • userID - User identifier (used only for maintenance_note URL)
  • noVerticalExtent - Flag only, values default to 0
  • noTaxa - Flag only, causes taxa removal
  • noPlatform - Flag only, affects platform/instrument structure

docs.title: Validation and Quality Control
docs.text:
The transformation includes several quality control measures:

  1. Empty Value Removal: All empty strings, nulls, and empty objects removed
  2. Type Conversion: String numbers converted to floats for coordinates/extents
  3. Coordinate Validation: Lat/long order corrected for standards compliance
  4. Date Extraction: Datetime strings normalized to date-only format where needed
  5. Whitespace Trimming: Keywords cleaned of leading/trailing spaces
  6. None Filtering: None values removed from concatenations

docs.title: Standards Compliance
docs.text: The CIOOS intermediate format is designed to support: - ISO 19115-3: Geographic information metadata - DataCite 4.5: Research data citation - ACDD 1.3: Attribute Convention for Data Discovery - Schema.org: Structured data for web discovery - CIOOS Metadata Profile: Canadian ocean data requirements

docs.title: CIOOS Form to DataCite Schema Mapping
docs.text: This document describes how metadata fields from the CIOOS Form are mapped to the DataCite Metadata Schema v4.5.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The conversion process follows two steps: 1. CIOOS Form to CIOOS: CIOOS Form data is converted to an intermediate CIOOS format (firebase_to_cioos.py) 2. CIOOS to DataCite: The CIOOS format is then mapped to DataCite schema (datacite.py)

docs.title: 1. Identifier (DOI)
docs.text: DataCite: identifier (identifierType="DOI") CIOOS Source: record['identification']['identifier'] CIOOS Form Source: datasetIdentifier Notes: - DOI prefix "https://doi.org/" is stripped - Can be optionally generated if doi_prefix parameter is provided

docs.title: 2. Creators
docs.text: DataCite: creators CIOOS Source: record['contact'] where inCitation = true CIOOS Form Source: contacts array Mapping Logic: - Filters contacts where inCitation is true - Personal creators: - creatorName: individual.name or concatenation of givenNames + lastName - nameType: "Personal" - givenName: individual.givenNames - familyName: individual.lastName - nameIdentifier: individual.orcid (if present) - nameIdentifierScheme: "ORCID" - schemeUri: "https://orcid.org" - Organization creators: - creatorName: organization.name - nameType: "Organizational" - lang: "en" - Affiliation (both types): - affiliation.name: organization.name - affiliationIdentifier: organization.ror (if present) - affiliationIdentifierScheme: "ROR" - schemeUri: "https://ror.org/"

docs.title: 3. Titles
docs.text: DataCite: titles CIOOS Source: record['identification']['title'] CIOOS Form Source: title (multilingual object with en, fr keys) Mapping Logic: - Each language becomes a separate title entry - titleType: "TranslatedTitle" - lang: Language code - Excludes "translations" metadata key

docs.title: 4. Publisher
docs.text: DataCite: publisher CIOOS Source: record['contact'] where 'publisher' in roles CIOOS Form Source: contacts array with role containing "publisher" Mapping Logic: - Uses organization name from first contact with publisher role - Falls back to "CIOOS" if no publisher found - publisherIdentifier: organization.ror (if present) - publisherIdentifierScheme: "ROR" - schemeUri: "https://ror.org/" - lang: "en"

docs.title: 5. Publication Year
docs.text: DataCite: publicationYear CIOOS Source: record['metadata']['dates']['publication'] CIOOS Form Source: timeFirstPublished Mapping Logic: - Extracts year from ISO date string - Falls back to current year if not available

docs.title: 6. Resource Type
docs.text: DataCite: types.resourceTypeGeneral CIOOS Source: record.get('metadataScope', 'Dataset') CIOOS Form Source: metadataScope or metadataScopeIso Default: "Dataset"

docs.title: 7. Subjects
docs.text:
DataCite: subjects Sources: Multiple Mapping Logic: - Fixed Subject: Always includes "FOS: Earth and related environmental sciences" - subjectScheme: "Fields of Science and Technology (FOS)" - schemeUri: "https://www.oecd.org/science/inno/38235147.pdf"

  • EOV (Essential Ocean Variables):
  • CIOOS Source: record['metadata']['eov']
  • CIOOS Form Source: eov array
  • Converted from camelCase to Title Case
  • subjectScheme: "GOOS EOV"

  • schemeUri: "https://www.goosocean.org/eov"

  • Keywords:

  • CIOOS Source: record['metadata']['keywords']
  • CIOOS Form Source: keywords.en and keywords.fr
  • No specific scheme assigned

docs.title: 8. Contributors
docs.text:
DataCite: contributors CIOOS Source: record['contact'] CIOOS Form Source: contacts array Mapping Logic: - All contacts except those with role "publisher" - Same personal/organization structure as creators - Role Mapping (CONTRIBUTOR_TYPE_MAPPING_FROM_CIOOS):

CIOOS Form Role DataCite Contributor Type pointOfContact ContactPerson distributor Distributor editor Editor rightsHolder RightsHolder sponsor Sponsor processor DataCurator metadataCustodian DataCurator custodian DataCurator owner RightsHolder funder Sponsor principalInvestigator ProjectLeader collaborator ProjectMember originator ProjectMember contributor ProjectMember author Researcher coAuthor Researcher mediator Other ressourceProvider Other stakeholder Other

Note: If no distributor is found in contacts, the system automatically adds the distributor role to the "owner" contact

docs.title: 9. Dates
docs.text:
DataCite: dates Mapping:

Date Type CIOOS Source CIOOS Form Source Created record['identification']['dates']['created'] Not directly mapped Updated record['metadata']['dates']['revision'] created (timestamp) Collected record['identification']['temporal_begin'] to record['identification']['temporal_end'] dateStart to dateEnd

Format: ISO 8601 date or date range (e.g., "2025-01-01/2025-03-01")

docs.title: 10. Language
docs.text: DataCite: language CIOOS Source: record['metadata']['language'] CIOOS Form Source: language

docs.title: 11. Alternate Identifiers
docs.text: DataCite: alternateIdentifiers Status: Currently empty array (placeholder)

docs.title: 12. Related Identifiers
docs.text: DataCite: relatedIdentifiers CIOOS Source: record['identification']['associated_resources'] CIOOS Form Source: associated_resources array Mapping: - relatedIdentifier: code (URL or DOI) - relatedIdentifierType: authority (e.g., "DOI", "URL") - relationType: association_type (e.g., "IsReferencedBy", "IsCitedBy")

docs.title: 13. Version
docs.text: DataCite: version CIOOS Source: record['identification']['edition'] CIOOS Form Source: edition

docs.title: 14. Rights List
docs.text: DataCite: rightsList CIOOS Source: record['metadata']['use_constraints']['licence'] CIOOS Form Source: license (code, e.g., "CC-BY-4.0") resolved via licenses.json Mapping: - rights: License title in English - rightsUri: License URL - rightsIdentifier: License code (e.g., "CC-BY-4.0") - rightsIdentifierScheme: "SPDX" - schemeUri: "https://spdx.org/licenses/" - lang: "en"

docs.title: 15. Descriptions
docs.text:
DataCite: descriptions Sources:

  1. Abstract:
  2. CIOOS Source: record['identification']['abstract']
  3. CIOOS Form Source: abstract (multilingual with en, fr)

  4. descriptionType: "Abstract"

  5. Limitations (if present):

  6. CIOOS Source: record['metadata']['use_constraints']['limitations']
  7. CIOOS Form Source: limitations
  8. descriptionType: "Other"
  9. Prefixed with "limitations: "

docs.title: 16. Geo Locations
docs.text:
DataCite: geoLocations Components:

  1. Bounding Box:
  2. CIOOS Source: record['spatial']['bounding_box']
  3. CIOOS Form Source: map.west, map.east, map.north, map.south

  4. Fields: westBoundLongitude, eastBoundLongitude, northBoundLatitude, southBoundLatitude

  5. Polygon (if present):

  6. CIOOS Source: record['spatial']['polygon']
  7. CIOOS Form Source: map.polygon
  8. Format: Space-separated coordinate pairs "lon,lat"

  9. Converted to array of polygonPoint with pointLongitude, pointLatitude

  10. Location Place:

  11. CIOOS Source: record['spatial']['description']['en']
  12. CIOOS Form Source: map.description.en
  13. Plain text place name

docs.title: 17. Funding References
docs.text: DataCite: fundingReferences CIOOS Source: record['contact'] where 'funder' in roles CIOOS Form Source: contacts with role containing "funder" Mapping: - funderName: organization.name - funderIdentifier: organization.ror (if present) - funderIdentifierType: "ROR"

docs.title: 18. Related Items
docs.text: DataCite: relatedItems Status: Currently empty array (placeholder)

docs.title: Additional Metadata in CIOOS (Not Mapped to DataCite)
docs.text:
The following fields are present in the CIOOS intermediate format but are not currently mapped to DataCite:

  • Spatial Information:
  • Vertical extent (min, max, direction, EPSG code)

  • Spatial description identifier

  • Identification:

  • Project information
  • Progress code

  • Status

  • Metadata:

  • Naming authority
  • Maintenance note
  • Comment

  • History/Lineage information

  • Platform and Instruments:

  • Platform details

  • Instrument information

  • Distribution:

  • Download URLs
  • Distribution descriptions

docs.title: 1. Coordinate Transformation
docs.text: Polygon coordinates are transformed from "lat,long" (CIOOS Form) to "long,lat" (CIOOS/DataCite standard).

docs.title: 2. EOV Translation
docs.text: EOV values are converted from camelCase to Title Case using the camel_to_title() utility function.

docs.title: 3. Taxa Formatting
docs.text: Taxa information is flattened from taxonomic hierarchy to a comma-separated list of taxonomic levels.

docs.title: 4. Empty Field Handling
docs.text: The conversion process includes scrubbing functions to remove empty strings, null values, and empty objects.

docs.title: 5. Deduplication
docs.text: Subjects and other repeating fields are deduplicated using the _get_unique_dicts() function.
